title: jsonmode-token-boundary-fractional-emit-and-schema-reconciliation-harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a focused test harness and runbook that exercises failure modes where JSON-mode structured output breaks due to partial-token emissions in streaming responses and tokenizer mismatches across model variants. The goal is to validate and harden our constrained-decoder + streaming reassembly logic and to codify recovery heuristics (repair-on-emit, token-aware boundary stitching, and schema-reconciliation fallbacks) so production clients see predictable behavior and clear telemetry when degradation occurs.
test_matrix: Partial-token emits: model returns half of a UTF-8 multi-byte char or a subword piece inside a JSON string field (simulate byte-level streaming truncation)
Interleaved toolcall markers: tool call indicators inserted and then cut mid-token to verify gate logic doesn't mis-interpret schema tokens
KV-cache mismatch: concurrent Batching where one shard uses a slightly different tokenizer/config causing merged stream to contain incompatible token boundaries
Quantization noise / sampling jitter: low-temp sampling leads to trailing commas or extra escapes that break strict JSON parsers
Legacy client compatibility: older SDKs performing incremental JSON-append parsing should hit graceful degradation path (partial-emit sentinel + resume) rather than fatal parse error

Fallback chain: constrained-decoder backoff -> soft-relaxation (allow trailing commas / missing closing bracket) -> canonical-rewrite attempt -> hard-fallback to text-mode with structured error envelope
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness reproduces at least 90% of injected partial-token failure modes deterministically in CI using our streaming simulator
Constrained-decoder path with token-boundary repair reduces parser-fatal failures by >= 75% on synthetic corpus compared to baseline
Telemetry events emitted for each repair/fallback with standardized tags (repair.type, repair.stage, original-token-fragment) and counts surfaced on Console dashboard
Runbook documented with clear mitigations and PR templates for runtime code changes; one on-call drill executed with SRE to validate observability
Compatibility tests included for two legacy SDK versions and one private-deployment quirk (non-UTF8 stream emulation)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use streaming-sim tool to emit model tokens with controlled cut points inside JSON string fields
2) Run constrained-decoder in strict mode and assert parser error is raised at stream reassembly boundary
3) Enable token-boundary-repair and confirm the same input yields a recoverable stream and valid JSON message
4) Run the legacy SDK JSON-append parser against both streams and verify the legacy path transitions to degrade mode instead of throwing
5) Execute the end-to-end embedding: client -> API gateway -> runtime shard mix (simulate KV mismatch) -> observe telemetry tags and counts
implementation_notes: Harness should be injectable into current JSON-mode e2e suite and run as a separate CI job that can be toggled via environment flags
Token-aware repair module must expose an instrumentation hook that returns the original fragments and the repaired bytes for reproducible replay
Prefer non-invasive runtime changes: introduce repair as a gating layer after streaming reassembly but before final constrained-decode pass
Add feature flag runtime.jsonmode.repair.enable to allow canary rollout and metric comparisons
Coordinate with tokenizer team for tests that cover both BPE and byte-level tokenizers, include round-trip fixtures
